posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
SCH1MakeIt said:
but i trying to make plugin alternate only LAN, and because that i please to Chatgpt to create the code it but not really work yet.
Click to expand...
That makes sense. See AI as a co-pilot. Only give it instructions that you could have made yourself but with the goal to save time and work more efficiently. A plane pilot gives commands to his co-pilot because he needs assistance, not because he wouldn't be able to fly the plane at all.
Back to topic:
Multiplayer is not something I would recommend doing in RPG Maker. It's simply not the engine for it. Image the next step, that could be combining an ABS plugin with multiplayer support: Just because you have plugin A and plugin B in your game, does NOT mean they magically work together. You would need a whole team for that, and the question would still be: Why with RPG Maker?

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
We, as plugin developers, are usually open to support beginners but only when they are willing to learn. We are not here to spend time investigating why AI didn't succeed with your prompt.
Buddy, start with something simple. RPG Makers has a full in-house battle system with buffs, debuffs, states, elemental rules, skills that get unlocked by picking up special weapons or armors, ... why not just make a short game to learn the basics?

posts.author: Synrec
posts.body:
If you want multiplayer in RPG Maker MV or MZ, you need to understand how NodeJS works on the server side and how it works (Or not) on the client side. You will need to create two projects basically.
The first RPG Maker project will be the server application. You can create maps to serve to the client, create the database, esentially, you can build the entire game server side. For hosting, you will need to deploy your RPG Maker server project as a NodeJS server. This is simple enough to do with express. And you will also need to create valid end points, learn cyber security and API access (If doing online instead of LAN)
Once the server is complete, the client is much simpler but also, more complex because at this point, you do not need most of RPG Maker scripts, functions or maps. Data must be gained from the server and loaded as an RPG Maker project. With synchronization with server of course. Cyber security would come from not abusing evals in the client <=>server interactions amongst other things if doing online.
I haven't truly stepped into multiplayer but please understand it's not as simple as slapping it into an AI and expecting it to work. It can be catastrophic, especially if doing online and can open yourself to litigation in severe cases.
